finding: Official plugin 22.0.1 zonedSchedule installs an alarm and saves pending notification data; channel creation occurs in createNotification when delivery/show runs. Product initialization previously did not explicitly register habit_reminders.

fix.behavior: Register the existing habit_reminders channel after plugin initialization, before launch handling and access diagnostics.

fix.existingChannelPolicy: Same ID and original values; no deletion or replacement; Android retains user importance, sound and vibration choices.
fix.permissionPolicy: Initialization does not request notification permission.
fix.failurePolicy: Registration failure makes readAccess unavailable; failed initialization can retry. Scheduler errors remain separate from committed habit facts.

targetedTests.command: flutter test --no-pub test/reminder_channel_initialization_test.dart test/reminder_access_test.dart test/reminder_recovery_test.dart test/reminder_status_test.dart --reporter expanded
newBehaviors: First access registers a settings channel before any notification is delivered.
Scheduled notification channel properties match the registered original properties.
A new service instance preserves user-disabled importance and sound/vibration choices; scheduling remains blocked.
A new service instance preserves user-low importance and sound/vibration choices while reminders can schedule.
Channel registration leaves app permission denied and makes no implicit permission request.
Registration failure reports unavailable; a later initialization retries successfully.

Actual disk SQLite facts survive channel registration failure, controller/repository close and reopen; habit, reminder time, completion, note and serialized snapshot are retained; registration recovery rebuilds reminders without changing stored facts.

limitations: Android notification transport uses the actual Flutter plugin serializer/parser against a MethodChannel native model. Host tests do not execute Android NotificationManager or the native system-settings UI.
Existing-channel preservation is grounded in Android official API behavior; device-side validation remains with the follow-up Android acceptance run.
No claim is made about the earlier API36 raw channel array or importance solely from source inspection.
No Go, AVD, Docker, app installation, publication, real server or secret access was performed.
Full test suite and debug build are coordinated by the parent task.
